newsitem.title: USA: Connie Lee chief says to oversee transition period.
newsitem.headline: Connie Lee chief says to oversee transition period.

text.p: Oliver Sockwell, president and chief executive officer of Connie Lee Insurance Co, said he would stay at the firm at least through the summer to oversee a possible sale of the company and the selection of a new CEO.

Sockwell announced in April he would retire July 1, but since that time the municipal bond insurance company said it received expressions of interest from entities interested in purchasing Connie Lee.
Sockwell said in a telephone interview that, as founder of the company, he was the best person to guide Connie Lee during its review of those proposals.

"It's been my position that I would stay as long as it took to effect a smooth transition to either a new CEO or to a new owner," Sockwell said. "We're learning as we go along how long that process might be. I really don't think the process will be longer than the end of this summer, but I started this place and I'm committed to do whatever's necessary, whatever's reasonable, to effect a smooth transition."
Sockwell said he expected the reviews would take only a few months.

Congress in 1987 created Connie Lee, also known as the Construction Loan Insurance Corp, to insure education bonds whose credit characteristics did not meet the requirements of private insurance companies. The company earlier this year completed a privatization that allows it to insure bonds from all sectors of the municipal market.
Sockwell said Connie Lee is in the "early stages" of evaluating potential new CEOs, and have "very attractive, seasoned, highly-accomplished people" who have indicated interest in the job.

Sockwell said the selection of a new CEO would not be consummated until the firm determined whether there would be a purchase. But he said both evaluation processes would be taking place along "parallel tracks" that he envisioned would be finished sometime later this summer.

"I still plan to retire," Sockwell said. "I'm just trying to assure that there's a smooth transition. I will remain on the board, but it's not a burden for me to stay on a couple more months if it makes sense for the company."
